tour.description: Velet is a payment and wallet core infrastructure for consistency-heavy money movement: identity, wallet balance management, and payment reservation/confirmation between users and merchants. Start with the README overview (scope, architecture, core patterns, tech stack), then the root Maven reactor (pom.xml), the two compose stacks (app infra plus observability), the init_db.sql bootstrap, and the five Spring Boot entry points (Gateway, Identity, Payment API, Payment Worker, Wallet) that map the whole system.
tour.title: Project overview and service map

tour.description: Spring Cloud Gateway is the single entry point routing to Identity, Payment, and Wallet. GatewayApplication bootstraps the edge service; application.yaml holds route definitions; AuthFilter validates JWTs on each request; KycGrantedFilter enforces KYC-gated access; SecurityAppProperties carries the security configuration properties the filters consult.
tour.title: Gateway entry and routing

tour.description: Identity owns login/register flows and JWT issuance. AuthenticationController exposes the auth endpoints; AuthenticationServiceImpl implements credential checking and token issuance; JwtUtil handles token creation/parsing; SecurityConfig wires the filter chain and access rules. Follow a register/login request from controller through service to token utilities.
tour.title: Identity and auth

tour.description: Wallet is the ledger-as-source-of-truth core with Redis as read-through cache. WalletController serves public balance/transfer endpoints while WalletInternalController exposes synchronous internal APIs called by payment over HTTP. Wallet, LedgerEntry, Transaction, and BalanceReservation model accounts and money movement; WalletRepository, LedgerRepository, and TransactionRepository persist them; WalletDomainService holds balance invariants and WalletApplicationService orchestrates use cases.
tour.title: Wallet core and ledger model

tour.description: Payments run as saga choreography (Reserve-Confirm-Release) with no central orchestrator. PaymentController receives create/status calls; PaymentServiceImpl (payment-api) persists Payment plus transactional-outbox rows; WalletClient/WalletRestClient make the synchronous wallet HTTP call; PaymentCreatedConsumer receives the created event in payment-worker; PaymentProcessingHandler and PaymentServiceImpl (worker) advance Reserve toward Confirm or Release, consulting wallet and merchant over HTTP.
tour.title: Payment saga flow

tour.description: Reliability comes from the transactional outbox plus RabbitMQ with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for safe concurrent polling. OutboxPoller (payment-worker and wallet) claims unpublished rows without lock contention; OutboxRepository backs the claim queries; RabbitMQConfig (payment-api and payment-worker) declares exchanges and templates; PaymentConsumerConfig and WalletExchangeConfig wire wallet-side bindings; PaymentEventListener applies confirmed/cancelled payment outcomes to wallet state.
tour.title: Async reliability: outbox and messaging

tour.description: Each service owns its Postgres schema managed by Flyway. The three V1 init-schema tables define identity, payment, and wallet DDL (including outbox, ledger, and reservation structures); the wallet and identity seed files provide test and benchmark data. Read schemas first, then seeds, to see how ledger, outbox, and user tables are initialized per service.
tour.title: Data and migrations

tour.description: Full tracing and metrics ride on OpenTelemetry across all services. The OTEL collector config, Prometheus scrape config, Tempo config, and Grafana datasource provisioning define the observability pipeline (brought up via docker-compose.obs.yml); the per-service application.yaml files show how identity, wallet, payment-api, and payment-worker point at Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ, and the OTEL endpoint operationally.
tour.title: Observability and ops
